newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wages boost Australian GDP outlook.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wages boost Australian GDP outlook.

text.p: Expectations of Australian December quarter GDP growth rose on Thursday with the release of higher-than-expected quarterly wages growth, analysts said.
November earnings wages data implied that wages, salaries and supplements would contribute around 0.7 percentage points to nominal (before inflation) expenditure-based estimate of GDP (GDP-E).
Economists had typically expected a contribution near 0.4 percentage points.

However, some economists said there were are a number of different methods of calculating the same figure and the result would depend, for example, on whether employment is broken down into full and part-time components and whether the labour force data is adjusted for methodological distortions admitted by the Australian Bureau of Statistics.
If the full and part-time components is ignored and the workforce is adjusted for the methodological change, then a contribution of 0.5 percentage points appears.

If full and part-timers are calculated separately and different measures used for the wage rates they were paid, as Access Economics analyst Chris Richardson did, then the 0.7 percentage point contribution appears.
However, Richardson said he did not allow for the bureau's understatement of employment growth.
The bureau acknowledges that a change to telephone interviewing has led to its monthly labour force understating employment growth since August by 6,000 to 9,000 a month.
